candidates.name: Nakasu Yatai
candidates.reason: Most photographed/famous yatai cluster, but two independent local sources describe it as catering to sightseeing groups with noticeably inflated prices and a rushed, crowded feel — the tourist-trap version of the exact experience this group's stated niche interest (yatai etiquette) wants to route around.

candidates.name: Nagahama Yatai
candidates.reason: Best pocket for the ramen-stall version of yatai specifically; corroborated as the most local of the three main districts.

candidates.name: Hakata Yatai Yokocho Kizuimaru
candidates.reason: Indoor, all-weather mini-yatai space (6 stalls, ~10 seats each) that runs a 'taisho experience' group course for 7+ people — a direct answer to the real logistics problem a party of 8 has at an actual street yatai (which seat ~10 total and expect groups to ask first / split up). Shipped with a recheck flag: an aggregator listing separately noted a since-unconfirmed March 2026 renovation closure that the operator's own site does not currently reflect.

candidates.name: Ichiran
candidates.reason: Two independent local sources (a resident forum thread and a local food blogger) describe Ichiran as pricier 'creative ramen' that doesn't fit the traditional Hakata/Nagahama/Kurume tonkotsu styles; residents default to cheaper, more traditional shops. Fails the bar as the generic default pick.

candidates.name: Shin-Shin
candidates.reason: Founder trained across multiple Fukuoka yatai before opening in 2004; known locally for a lighter ('assari') tonkotsu broth distinct from the heavier tourist-chain norm, with a Tenjin honten that draws consistent local lines rather than only tour groups.

candidates.name: Motsunabe Kobayashi
candidates.reason: Direct fit for this exact party size: the operator's own site advertises an all-you-can-drink motsunabe course with the organizer's meal free for parties of 8+, online booking available, 5 minutes from Nishitetsu Tenjin Station.

candidates.name: Motsu Shigeru
candidates.reason: Michelin-recognized, deeply loved locally for a motsu-sukiyaki twist on the standard dish — genuinely excellent per local sources, but no group-size incentive or clear large-party online booking path surfaced within this pass's budget. Worth remembering for a smaller-subgroup dinner rather than the full party of 8.

candidates.name: Komyozenji
candidates.reason: Genuinely quieter, moss-garden alternative literally next door to Dazaifu Tenmangu's crowds — but a maintained English travel reference (updated 2025) currently describes it as not regularly open to the public, consistent with several 2021-2023 firsthand reports of an unexpectedly closed gate. Ship only as a zero-detour 'check on arrival' peek, never as a planned stop.

candidates.name: Oguchi Beach
candidates.reason: Aggregator-listed as a quieter alternative to Futamigaura ~10 minutes away, but a second independent search collided with an unrelated Shima (Mie Prefecture) region and produced no genuine second corroborating source for the 'quieter' claim within this pass's budget. Left as an unproven lead, not shipped.

candidates.name: Dazaifu Liner Bus Tabito
candidates.reason: Direct, no-transfer alternative to the standard Nishitetsu Tenjin→Futsukaichi→Dazaifu train transfer, departing Hakata Bus Terminal (and Fukuoka Airport) — relevant if the group's lodging sits nearer Hakata Station than Tenjin.

evidence.claim: Compared to Tenjin, Nakasu's yatai cater more heavily to sightseeing/tour groups, with noticeably inflated prices and a busier, less conversational atmosphere.

A yatai stall seats roughly 10 people total; the expected etiquette for a large party is to ask the owner before sitting, order at least one item per person, and keep the visit brief so seats turn over for other customers rather than spreading out or lingering.

Hakata Yatai Yokocho Kizuimaru (Daimyo 1-8-31, Libertus Daimyo 1F; 5 min walk from Akasaka Station) is an indoor, all-weather yatai-style space with 6 mini-stalls of ~10 seats each; open 12:00-23:00 (food L.O. 22:00, drinks L.O. 22:30), closed Wednesdays.

A booking-aggregator listing (hotpepper.jp) separately states this venue was closing 2026-03-22 for renovation; the operator's own site, fetched 2026-08-29, shows normal current hours with no closure notice, and a 2026-08-13 local-news write-up (fanfun.jp) describes it as an active, ongoing feature. The renovation note is not corroborated elsewhere and could be stale aggregator data — reconfirm by phone (092-791-3090) close to the trip date rather than assuming either signal.

Motsunabe Kobayashi (Imaizumi 1-13-5, Burg Imaizumi 2F, 5 min walk from Nishitetsu Tenjin south exit) runs an all-you-can-drink motsunabe full course (8 dishes) at ¥4,850/person with the organizer's meal free for parties of 8 or more; open 17:00-01:00 daily, online booking available.

Fukuya, founded 1949 in Nakasu, was the first company to commercially sell mentaiko in Japan and remains closely tied to the local Hakata community (its founder helped establish the Nakasu contingent of the Hakata Gion Yamakasa festival) — a locally-rooted pick rather than only an airport souvenir brand.
Dazaifu Tenmangu opens 6:00 (spring equinox–day before autumn equinox) or 6:30 (rest of year); in October it closes 19:00. No admission fee for the shrine grounds.
Dazaifu Tenmangu is markedly quieter before roughly 9:00-10:00 and after about 16:00; weekday mornings are the best combination for avoiding both crowds and tour groups.

Komyozenji's interior and moss garden are, per a maintained English-language travel reference last updated 2025-02-25, 'currently not regularly open to the public' — no fixed hours or admission fee are publishable while this stands; several 2021-2023 visitor accounts independently describe finding the gate closed on arrival.

When Komyozenji is open, the atmosphere is markedly calmer than Dazaifu Tenmangu next door — visitors describe foot traffic dropping considerably just by stepping off the main shrine approach onto the temple's path.

The Fukuoka municipal ferry from Meinohama to Nokonoshima runs 23 sailings/day (5:00-22:45, one early sailing suspended on Sundays/holidays), a 10-minute crossing, ¥230 one-way adult fare, first-come first-served with no reservations.

The bus connecting Tenjin/Hakata to Meinohama pier runs far less often than the ferry itself — roughly 1-2/hour, worse on weekends — so the bus leg, not the ferry, is the tighter connection to plan around; the ferry can also fill past capacity on a busy holiday, occasionally leaving a queue for the next sailing.

Itoshima's own tourism association describes local bus frequency as 'extremely limited' with no loop route linking the peninsula's scattered sights (flat ¥200 fare); it recommends compact taxis (max 4 passengers) to fill gaps, meaning a party of 8 needs two taxis together, and notes hourly-rental sightseeing-taxi packages exist for cost-sharing groups.

The Nishitetsu 'Tabito' liner bus runs direct from Hakata Bus Terminal (1F, bay 11) to Dazaifu with no transfer — 40 minutes, ¥800 (¥20 off with IC/credit), 28 weekday / 36 weekend-holiday trips each direction; also runs from Fukuoka Airport (25 min, ¥700). No reservation required, capacity-dependent boarding.

Sakurai Futamigaura's iconic sunset-between-the-rocks view draws heavy crowds and full parking, especially around the summer solstice and on weekend/holiday evenings; arriving at least an hour before sunset (or visiting midday instead of at sunset, or choosing a weekday) is how locals avoid the worst of it.

reservations.partyRules: 8+ diners qualifies for the organizer-free motsunabe course (¥4,850/head, all-you-can-drink included); course pricing is per person, confirm exact headcount at booking.
reservations.foreignFriction: Booking interface and phone line appear Japanese-only; no English support evidence found — hotel concierge or a Japanese-speaking call may be needed.
reservations.lastSeating: Food L.O. 24:00, drinks L.O. 24:30; open 17:00-01:00, so a late group dinner is workable.
reservations.walkIn: Not evaluated this pass — treat as reservation-recommended for a party of 8.
reservations.alternatives: Motsu Shigeru (Akasaka, Michelin-recognized, motsu-sukiyaki twist) and Yamachuu (locally rated for the richest broth) are strong smaller-subgroup alternatives; neither had group-size reservation depth researched this pass.

reservations.releaseWindow: Reservation required by the day before the visit (前日までに予約が必要), by phone only.
reservations.partyRules: The 'taisho experience' group course requires a minimum of 7 guests (adults or elementary-age children).
reservations.foreignFriction: Phone-only booking (092-791-3090) in Japanese; no online reservation channel found on the operator's own site — real friction for a foreign group, plan for hotel-concierge assistance.
reservations.walkIn: The venue has 6 indoor stalls seating ~10 each (60 total); a walk-in party of 8 could plausibly fit at one stall for a normal (non-course) meal without the group reservation, but this was not independently confirmed.

leads.claim: Taisho-experience group course priced at ¥5,000/adult (7+ people), with all-you-can-drink plus all-you-can-eat mentaiko and a free happi-coat 'taisho' role-play for one designated member, per aggregator listings (hotpepper.jp, fanfun.jp).

reservations.alternatives: A real Tenjin street-yatai crawl split into two sub-groups of ~4 is the more 'authentic' version of this experience, at the cost of the group not sharing one table.
reservations.fallback: If closed or unavailable, Motsunabe Kobayashi's organizer-free 8+ course is a full-group alternative that doesn't depend on yatai seating limits.

transport.route: Fukuoka city → Itoshima Peninsula sights (Sakurai Futamigaura area, coastal cafes) via Showa Bus + local taxi
transport.doorToDoor: No single loop connects the peninsula's scattered sights; expect a bus leg plus taxi legs between stops, on the order of 60-90+ minutes door-to-door depending on the starting point in Fukuoka city.
transport.transferReality: Itoshima's community buses are fixed-schedule, point-to-point routes (not a loop) at a flat ¥200 fare; some stops only serve one direction, and the peninsula is 'unexpectedly sprawling' per its own tourism association.
transport.groupLuggageMobility: Local taxis are compact (max ~4 passengers), so a party of 8 needs two taxis coordinated together for any taxi leg — not a solo/small-group ride; hourly-rental sightseeing-taxi packages exist and may suit a group better than metered point-to-point fares.
transport.buffer: Build slack around each bus connection rather than chaining tight transfers; the tourism association itself frames bus frequency as a planning constraint, not routine city transit.
transport.missedConnection: Missing a connecting bus on a sparse route can mean a long wait for the next one; not independently pinned to an exact worst-case interval this pass.
transport.nextService: Not uniformly confirmed across all routes this pass — flag ⚠ and check the specific route's timetable for the travel date.
transport.lastPracticalReturn: Not independently confirmed this pass — flag ⚠ and check the same-day last bus/taxi availability before heading out, especially for a sunset visit to Futamigaura.
transport.fallback: Treat two coordinated taxis as the default connector between clustered stops rather than relying on bus transfers for a multi-stop day; whether a rental car is realistic for this group is a question for Pass A / reconcile.

transport.route: Meinohama Pier (Fukuoka city) → Nokonoshima Island via the Fukuoka municipal ferry
transport.doorToDoor: Bus from Tenjin (~30 min) or Hakata (~40 min) to Meinohama pier, then a 10-minute ferry crossing.
transport.transferReality: Ferry runs 23 sailings/day (5:00-22:45), no reservations, first-come first-served boarding; the connecting bus from Tenjin/Hakata to the pier is the tighter link at roughly 1-2/hour.
transport.groupLuggageMobility: Ferry capacity comfortably absorbs a party of 8; watch the bus leg instead.
transport.missedConnection: A missed ferry means waiting for the next of 23 daily sailings — low-stakes on a normal day; a busy holiday can fill a sailing past capacity per local reports.
transport.nextService: Roughly every 30-60 minutes depending on time of day.
transport.lastPracticalReturn: Last ferry ~22:45, but Nokonoshima Island Park's own facilities close much earlier — plan around the park's hours, not the ferry's (park hours not verified this pass).

saturation.note: Late-round searches (yatai cash-only corroboration, a second 'quieter than Futamigaura' beach corroboration, a Kizuimaru official course subpage) returned either duplicate framing, an unrelated region (Shima, Mie Prefecture, confused with Itoshima's Shima district), or dead pages. Priority coverage — yatai crowd/group-size reality, ramen and motsunabe local-vs-tourist picks matched to an 8-person party, a Dazaifu crowd-avoidance alternative (with its access caveat caught rather than glossed over), and Itoshima/Nokonoshima transit reality — is corroborated from independent source families. Remaining open threads (Kizuimaru's exact post-renovation status, Komyozenji's access unpredictability, Itoshima's exact bus timetable) are flagged with recheck dates rather than blocking; resolving them would refine timing and confidence, not flip which candidates are worth recommending.
